inotify_bridge.method: bellocode-exec in ~/.bellocode-g6-spike/bench; inotifywait -m in the container; host writes; then an in-container `touch -c`
inotify_bridge.host_create_and_modify: no inotify events in the container
inotify_bridge.in_container_touch_c: ATTRIB event delivered for the touched file
inotify_bridge.conclusion: host edits (the agent's file tools) do not wake watchers inside the container; a host FSEvents -> batched `touch -c` exec bridge, or polling watchers (CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=1, WATCHPACK_POLLING=true), is needed for hot reload

git_worktree_in_container.method: host `git worktree add` under opencode's worktree directory (mounted at the same path); git in the container
git_worktree_in_container.gitdir_file: absolute host path (.../proj/.git/worktrees/feature), resolves in the container because paths match
git_worktree_in_container.git_status: fails: 'detected dubious ownership' (host-created directories can appear as uid 0 inside the container)
git_worktree_in_container.git_commit_in_worktree: works; the commit is visible to host git

ownership_inside_container: files and directories created on the host appear as uid 501 or uid 0 inside the container depending on the directory; files created in the container (as uid 501 or as root) appear on the host as the host user (uid 501, gid 20)
umask: files created by an exec get mode 0666 on the host: set umask 022 in the wrapper
published_ports: HostIp 127.0.0.1 -> limactl listens on 127.0.0.1 only; HostIp 0.0.0.0 -> limactl listens on *:port (every interface of the Mac)
seq_note: host /usr/bin/seq (BSD) prints large numbers differently from GNU seq, so the byte counts differ; throughput compares time only
